advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile `_CHECKBOX_STATE_RE` with the canonical AC checkbox grammar (`_plan_clarity._CHECKBOX_RE`) so the fingerprint normalizer and close-precheck share one definition of a checkbox.
evidence: _plan_clarity.py:17 `_CHECKBOX_RE = re.compile(r"^- \[( |x|X)\](?:[ \t]+(.*))?$")` — canonical AC grammar is hyphen-only, no indent, single space
decide.py:237 `if text[:1] in "-*+":` — the finding-marker stripper treats `+` as a bullet too, which the fingerprint normalizer does not
advisory.finding: The fingerprint checkbox grammar `_CHECKBOX_STATE_RE = ^(\s*[-*]\s*\[)[xX ](\])` diverges from the two other checkbox notions in the codebase — the canonical AC parser `^- \[( |x|X)\]` (hyphen-only, no indent, single space) and the finding-marker stripper that accepts `-`/`*`/`+` bullets — creating three inconsistent definitions of 'a checkbox'. The normalizer accepts leading indent and `*` but not `+`; if the canonical AC grammar ever widens, box flips on newly-accepted forms could silently re-diverge and reintroduce spurious stale-material.
scenarios: A future edit that broadens the canonical AC checkbox grammar (e.g. to accept `+` bullets or indentation) without updating this normalizer would let those flips move the fingerprint again.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a fingerprint test that a non-checkbox `[x]`/`[ ]` bracket token in description prose is preserved as material (editing it moves the fingerprint), pinning the regex bullet-anchor against over-normalization.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:740: `_CHECKBOX_STATE_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*[-*]\s*\[)[xX ](\])", re.MULTILINE)` — the bullet anchor is the sole thing keeping prose `[x]` tokens material.

tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1017-1039: the three new fingerprint tests only exercise `- [x]`/`* [x]` at real bullet positions; `test_material_fingerprint_item_text_edit_still_changes` edits the item WORD ('another check'), not a bracketed token in prose.

ABSENCE: no assertion that `material_fingerprint(desc with 'see step [x] below')` differs when that prose `[x]` is edited, i.e. the regression that widens the anchor to swallow non-checkbox brackets is undetected.
advisory.finding: No test asserts the anchor-safety boundary of `_normalize_checkbox_state`: a `[x]`/`[ ]` bracket token NOT in checkbox position (inline prose, or not preceded by a `-`/`*` bullet) must be PRESERVED as material. Every test's checkbox sits at a proper bullet, so an over-normalization regression (widening the `^\s*[-*]\s*` anchor) would silently mask a material prose edit and keep a stale signature wrongly valid without any test failing.
scenarios: A refactor of `_CHECKBOX_STATE_RE` that drops or loosens the `[-*]` bullet anchor would normalize away any `[x]`/`[ ]` in description prose, causing a material edit to those lines to leave the fingerprint unchanged and keep a stale plan-review attestation valid.
An operator edits an AC line's bracketed material content (not a checkbox) after signing; the stale-material gate silently fails to fire.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test asserting `material_fingerprint(_ctx(base + '\nSee marker [ ] in text.'))` != `material_fingerprint(_ctx(base + '\nSee marker [x] in text.'))`, so a prose bracket flip (not at a bullet) still changes the fingerprint.
